newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares seen steady ahead of expiry.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares seen steady ahead of expiry.

text.p: Austrian shares closed barely changed on Wednesday after trading within a narrow range on low turnover.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips lost just 0.01 percent, or 0.11 points, to end at 1,213.69 with 10 shares advancing and 11 falling.

Traders see the ATX well supported at 1,210 points and expect the market to drift sideways ahead of the expiry of March futures and options contracts on Friday -- barring the emergence of fresh incentives.
"It's holding up very well between 1,210 and 1,215. We should be able to form a bottom at this level," said one trader.
The day's top performer was oil and chemicals group OMV, gaining 1.14 percent to 1,371 schillings, while the poorest was high-grade steelmaker Boehler, falling 1.53 percent to 806.5.
In the broader market, BWT, Europe's leading manufacturer of water-treatment technology, continued its strong performance, adding on three percent to 1,439 schillings.
BWT has climbed 9.7 percent since Friday, when it announced it had developed a new technology it expects will bring in substantial earnings in the next five years.
The all-share Vienna bourse closed 0.12 percent lower at 454.79 points.
The March ATX future shed one point to 1,213 on turnover of 3,009 contracts.
